quote.text: AI Assistant is the channel by which users arrive at your site from sources like ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Copilot, or Grok.

rule_quote.text: The medium is set to “ai-assistant” and the campaign is set to “(ai-assistant)” if the referrer matches a list of AI Assistants.

general_caveats: Native mobile/desktop assistant apps frequently send no Referer; such clicks look like Direct traffic (widely reported, not operator-confirmed).
Browsers' default Referrer-Policy (strict-origin-when-cross-origin) means only the origin, not the path, is normally sent cross-site; host-based matching is the reliable unit.
utm_source values are attacker-controllable query parameters; treat them as attribution hints, not authentication.

robots_rfc9309.rfc: RFC 9309, Robots Exclusion Protocol, Standards Track, September 2022 (Koster, Illyes, Zeller, Sassman)

quote.text: The product token MUST contain only uppercase and lowercase letters ("a-z" and "A-Z"), underscores ("_"), and hyphens ("-").

product_token_charset.implementation_rule: Valid tokens: [A-Za-z_-]+ (ABNF identifier = 1*(%x2D / %x41-5A / %x5F / %x61-7A)). Note: no digits allowed by the ABNF.

quote.text: Crawlers MUST use case-insensitive matching to find the group that matches the product token and then obey the rules of the group.

group_matching_case_insensitive.implementation_rule: Compare the user-agent line value to the crawler's product token case-insensitively (the RFC defines token equality, not prefix/substring matching of the line value).

quote.text: If there is more than one group matching the user-agent, the matching groups' rules MUST be combined into one group

merge_multiple_groups.implementation_rule: Union all rules from every group whose user-agent line matches the token, then evaluate as one group.

quote.text: If no matching group exists, crawlers MUST obey the group with a user-agent line with the "*" value, if present.

star_fallback.implementation_rule: Use '*' group(s) only when no specific group matches. Specific match fully replaces '*' (no inheritance).

quote.text: If no group matches the product token and there is no group with a user-agent line with the "*" value, or no groups are present at all, no rules apply.
The group is terminated by a user-agent line or end of file.

group_definition.implementation_rule: Consecutive user-agent lines share the following rules; a user-agent line after rules starts a new group. The last group may have no rules (allows everything).

quote.text: The most specific match found MUST be used. The most specific match is the match that has the most octets.

longest_match.implementation_rule: Among all allow/disallow rules whose pattern matches the path, pick the one with the most octets (pattern length).

quote.text: If an "allow" rule and a "disallow" rule are equivalent, then the "allow" rule SHOULD be used.

tie_break_allow.implementation_rule: On equal-length/equivalent match, allow wins (SHOULD, not MUST).

quote.text: If no match is found amongst the rules in a group for a matching user-agent or there are no rules in the group, the URI is allowed.
The /robots.txt URI is implicitly allowed.
The matching SHOULD be case sensitive. The matching MUST start with the first octet of the path.

match_from_start_case_sensitive.implementation_rule: Anchored prefix match on the path (incl. query), case-sensitive.

quote.text: Octets in the URI and robots.txt paths outside the range of the ASCII coded character set, and those in the reserved range defined by [RFC3986], MUST be percent-encoded

percent_encoding.implementation_rule: Normalise both sides: percent-encode non-ASCII/reserved, decode percent-encoded unreserved ASCII, before comparing.

quote.text: The crawler SHOULD ignore "disallow" and "allow" rules that are not in any group

rules_outside_groups.implementation_rule: Drop rules before the first user-agent line.

quote.text: Crawlers MUST support the following special characters:

wildcards.implementation_rule: '#' comment, '$' end-of-pattern anchor, '*' = 0 or more of any character (Figure 5). Literal * or $ in URIs should be %-encoded (%2A, %24).

quote.text: Parsing of other records MUST NOT interfere with the parsing of explicitly defined records in Section 2.

other_records.implementation_rule: e.g. a Sitemap line MUST NOT terminate a group.

quote.text: The rules MUST be accessible in a file named "/robots.txt" (all lowercase) in the top-level path of the service.
The crawlers SHOULD follow at least five consecutive redirects, even across authorities

redirects.implementation_rule: Follow >=5 redirects; apply fetched rules to the initial authority; >5 MAY be treated as unavailable.

quote.text: If a server status code indicates that the robots.txt file is unavailable to the crawler, then the crawler MAY access any resources on the server.
If the robots.txt file is unreachable due to server or network errors, this means the robots.txt file is undefined and the crawler MUST assume complete disallow.

status_5xx_unreachable.implementation_rule: HTTP 500-599 or network error => disallow all; after a 'reasonably long period' (e.g. 30 days) MAY treat as unavailable or keep using a cached copy.

quote.text: Crawlers MUST try to parse each line of the robots.txt file. Crawlers MUST use the parseable rules.

parsing_errors.implementation_rule: Skip unparseable lines; keep the rest.

quote.text: Crawlers SHOULD NOT use the cached version for more than 24 hours, unless the robots.txt file is unreachable.
The parsing limit MUST be at least 500 kibibytes [KiB].

size_limit.implementation_rule: CORRECTION to the brief: 500 KiB is a MINIMUM parsing limit, not a maximum file size. Parse at least the first 512,000 bytes; you MAY ignore content beyond your limit if limit >= 500 KiB.

examples.longest_match_5_2: User-Agent: foobot / Allow: /example/page/ / Disallow: /example/page/disallowed.gif -> the Disallow wins for /example/page/disallowed.gif (longer match).

items: 7124 (Sec 5.2): example text says URI '.../disallow.gif' but means '.../disallowed.gif'.
7128 (Sec 2.2.2): Figure 4 should say U+30C4, not U+E38384.
7995 (Sec 2.2): ABNF path-pattern requires leading '/', yet Sec 5.1 uses 'Disallow: *.gif$' -> accept patterns starting with '*'.
8895 (Sec 2.3.1.5, reported 2026-04-28 by Fabrice Canel): proposes OPTIONAL comma-separated user-agent lists ('User-agent: a, b'). Not part of the RFC.

operator_deviations_seen_in_part_A: Google: some crawlers have more than one token (e.g. Googlebot-Image also obeys Googlebot; Google-CloudVertexBot also obeys Googlebot) - 'you need to match only one crawler token for a rule to apply'.
Apple: if no Applebot group but a Googlebot group exists, Applebot follows the Googlebot group. Applebot ignores Crawl-delay.
Amazon: Amzn-SearchBot follows rules given to 'other search bots' if not named; unfetchable robots.txt treated as non-existent (contrast RFC 5xx => disallow all); cached copy up to 30 days.
Google special-case crawlers (e.g. APIs-Google, AdsBot) ignore the '*' group.

User-triggered fetchers (ChatGPT-User, Perplexity-User, Google user-triggered fetchers incl. Google-Agent, Meta-ExternalFetcher, Amzn-User) may ignore robots.txt per their operators; Anthropic's Claude-User and Mistral's MistralAI-User are documented as robots-governed.
Crawl-delay (non-standard): honored by ClaudeBot, CCBot, YouBot, Diffbot; not by Applebot or Amazon bots.
